newsitem.title: USA: USDA May 12 U.S. crop highlights--USDA.
newsitem.headline: USDA May 12 U.S. crop highlights--USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday issued its first projections for 1997 soybean and corn crops, pegging this year's U.S. soybean production at a record level of 2.600 billion bushels and corn at 9.840 billion bushels, the second largest corn crop on record.
The 1997 U.S. wheat crop was estimated at 2.261 billion bushels, down slightly from the previous year.

Winter wheat production, which normally accounts for over two-thirds of the total American wheat crop, was estimated at 1.561 billion bushels, six percent above last year's level of 1.478 billion bushels.
Frost damage last month in the major wheat producing states of Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas pared yields in those areas, but not as much as initially feared.
USDA projected the average U.S. soybean yield this year at 38.5 bushels per acre, second only to the record 41.4 bushels per acre in 1994/95.
Soybean ending stocks for 1996/97 were left unchanged at the 20-year low level of 125 million bushels but were projected to rebound next year to 260 million bushels.
Last year U.S. farmers harvested 2.382 billion bushels of soybeans. The largest U.S. soybean crop was produced in 1994 and totalled 2.517 billion bushels.
U.S. corn production last year totalled 9.293 billion bushels, compared to the record production in 1994 of 10.103 billion.

The USDA corn and soybean projections were not based on farmer surveys, but were calculated from models assuming normal weather patterns in growing areas. The government will issue its first survey-based estimates for corn and soybeans in August.
